messages:
Ravi K: FYI — multiple customers reported that the Console's "view trace" link from Logs sometimes 404s or opens the wrong trace. Quick look shows logs arriving with mixed fields: `traceid`, `trace_id`, `traceId`, and sometimes only a `traceparent` header.

Olivia Chen: Do we have a small repro or example raw event?

Ravi K: Here are a couple of real snippets (redacted) I pulled from kinesis:```json
{
  "ts": "2026-03-16T18:22:10Z",
  "level": "info",
  "msg": "user checkout",
  "traceid": "4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736"
}
{
  "ts": "2026-03-16T18:22:11Z",
  "level": "info",
  "msg": "cart updated",
  "traceparent": "00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01"
}
{
  "ts": "2026-03-16T18:22:12Z",
  "level": "info",
  "msg": "payment started",
  "traceId": "4bf92f3577b34da6"  // 16-char variant
}
```

Jamie: This matches what I saw in staging — some SDKs send full 32-char trace-id, others are truncating or using 64-bit ids. Our linking code in Console expects the normalized 32-char lowercase hex in `trace_id`. If ingestion doesn't normalize, linking fails.

Mike P: If we normalize at ingest, watch cost/perf. Enrichment means touching every log — parsing, normalization, maybe extra indexing. Also need to be careful about accidentally promoting any PII that shows up near trace fields.

Olivia Chen: Alternatives: (A) require SDKs to log a `trace_id` field in our canonical format (32 lowercase hex) — minimal ingest work but requires app churn; (B) perform normalization in the log-forwarder/ingest pipeline so apps don't change. Which do we prefer?

Jamie: My take: do ingest-normalization as a short-term fix (zero touch for customers). Long-term: provide SDKs/formatters that emit canonical `trace_id`. Also we should canonicalize these names: accept `traceparent`, `traceid`, `traceId`, `trace_id` and map -> `trace_id`.

Mike P: Also normalize format: ensure 32-char lowercase hex. Some third-party libs output uppercase; some use 16 char. For 16-char variants, canonicalize to the 32-char by zero-left-padding or treat as short id and populate `trace_id_short` = last 16 hex for UI fallbacks. Must document rules.

Ravi K: Proposal for ingest pipeline work:
1) Detect and parse `traceparent` header if present and extract 32-char trace-id.
2) If only `traceId` / `traceid` present and length != 32, try to detect variant and convert; if ambiguous, mark `trace_id_normalized=false` and attach `trace_id_raw`.
3) Populate `trace_id` (32-lowercase), and `trace_id_short` (last 16) for fast lookup.
4) Emit metrics: `logs.trace.normalization.success` / `logs.trace.normalization.fail` by source.

Jamie: +1. Sample ingest rule (pseudo):```yaml
- match: any
  extract:`traceparent` -> trace_id
  fallback: fields[trace_id, traceid, traceId] -> trace_id_raw
  normalize: to_lowerhex(ensure_32) -> trace_id
  set: trace_id_short = trace_id[-16:]
```

Olivia Chen: Good. Two operational concerns: (1) perf impact for high-volume customers — we should make normalization opt-out per customer or gate it behind a CPU budget. (2) Retention/indexing cost — adding `trace_id` as an indexed field increases storage. Maybe index only for customers on Dedicated or those who opt-in.

Mike P: Agree. For Hosted customers we can default to create `trace_id` but not index it; for Dedicated we can index. Also ensure our exporters to downstream systems (es/elasticsearch, clickhouse) preserve the field naming contract.

Jamie: Also note exporters: our OTLP span exporter already normalizes spans' trace_id. The mismatch happens because logs go through a different path (fluent-bit -> kinesis -> ingest). Need a small shim in the log-ingest service that reuses span normalization logic to avoid duplication and bugs.

Ravi K: Security note — before enrichment ensure we run the PII scrub pipeline. If `trace_id` was accidentally attached to a PII-containing object we don't want to surface more context.

Olivia Chen: Plan: I'll draft an RFC with: scope, normalization rules, rollback plan, perf targets, and rollout steps (staging -> canary customers -> all). Owners: Olivia Chen (RFC + rollout), Jamie (ingest shim), Mike P (cost/retention plan), Ravi K (Console linking changes + metrics). Target: RFC by EOD Friday, light rollout the following week.

ingest-bot: created task INF-1234: "normalize-trace-fields" assigned to Olivia Chen, due 2026-03-20

Olivia Chen: tagging @eng-sre for perf review and @eng-platform for API/console changes. Anyone object to that plan?

Jamie: No objections. I'll start the shim PR and add perf benchmarks.

Mike P: :thumbsup:

Ravi K: Thanks — will add test cases to the Console linking unit tests for the various trace_id formats so we don't regress.
